Sweet potato is a root modification while potato is a stem modification but both of them have same function. Analogous structures are not anatomically similar structures though they perform similar functions.

Analogous structures are the result of convergent evolution.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Evolution of human appears parallel to the progressive development of brain and language skills. As such, the evolution of individual species in the sequence of their appearance is :
questions.solution:
The evolutionary sequence of human species in the order of their appearance is:

Ramapithecus (about 15 million years ago)
$\downarrow$
Australopithecus (about 2 million years ago)
$\downarrow$
Homo habilis (about 2 million years ago)
$\downarrow$
Homo erectus (about 1.5 million years ago)
$\downarrow$
Neanderthal man (100,000 - 40,000 years ago)
$\downarrow$
Homo sapiens (75,000 - 10,000 years ago)

Thus, the correct sequence is Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens.

Answer: Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : Forelimbs of human and bats are homologous.
Reason R : Forelimbs of humans and bats have similar anatomical structure.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\text{A}$
Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are true, but $\text{R}$ is not the correct explanation of $\text{A}$
questions.solution:
Homologous organs are those which have the same fundamental anatomical structure and embryonic origin but may perform different functions.

The forelimbs of humans and bats have the same basic structural plan, consisting of the humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, and phalanges. Because they share this similar anatomical structure, they are classified as homologous organs.

Thus, Assertion A is true, Reason R is true, and Reason R is the correct explanation for Assertion A.

Answer: Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\text{A}$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not evidence for evolution ?
options: Divergent evolution of anatomical structures such as forelimbs
Convergent evolution of traits like wings of birds and butterflies
Embryological support for evolution as proposed by Ernst Heckel
questions.solution:
Embryological support for evolution was proposed by Ernst Haeckel based on the observation of certain features during the embryonic stage common to all vertebrates that are absent in adults. However, this proposal was disapproved after careful study by Karl Ernst von Baer, who noted that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals. Therefore, the embryological support as proposed by Ernst Haeckel is not considered valid evidence for evolution.

Divergent evolution (homology), convergent evolution (analogy), and paleontological evidence (fossils) are all accepted evidences for evolution.

Answer: Embryological support for evolution as proposed by Ernst Heckel

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a living fossil?
questions.solution: Archaeopteryx is not a living fossil. It is a fossil bird which lived in the Jurassic period and is considered a connecting link between birds and reptiles. King crab (arthropoda), Sphenodon (reptile) and Peripatus (oviparous mammal) are living fossils.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following experiments suggests that simplest living organisms could not have originated spontaneously from non-living matter?
options: larvae could appear in decaying organic matter
microbes did not appear in stored meat
microbes appeared from unsterilized organic matter
meat was not spoiled, when heated and kept sealed in a vessel.
questions.solution:
The simplest living organisms could not have originated spontaneously from non-living matter. Microbes were killed by heating the meat and the sealed vessel formed a closed system wherein the new microbes could not come in contact with the nutrient medium and hence no spoilage of meat.
Related Theory
Pasteur performed experiments in which he took sterilized yeast and sugar solution in a long necked, then he bent the neck of the flask like a neck of swan. After one month he observed that no life appeared in flask solution because the curved flask neck acts as a filter. He later on broken down the neck and observed the solution. He found that many micro-organisms were originated in solution.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Industrial melanism as observed in peppered moth proves that:
options: the melanic form of the moth as no selective advantage over lighter form in industrial area.
the lighter-form moth has no selective advantage either in polluted industrial area or non-polluted area
the true black melanic forms arise by a recurring random
questions.solution:
Industrial melanism is a term used to describe the evolutionary process in which darker individuals came to predominate over lighter individuals because of the Industrial Revolution. This occurred as a result of natural selection in which a black 'melanic' form arose by a recurring random mutation, but its phenotypic appearance had a strong selective advantage in industrial areas.
Related Theory
During the period when the number of coal burning factories in England was increasing (during the so-called Industrial Revolution) it was noticed that the number of melanic individuals of the species of Peppered Moth (Biston betularia) was becoming more common. Originally rare in the population of normally light-coloured moths, the frequency of the melanic form increased in polluted areas until it was over $90 \%$. This change in colour has come to be known as "industrial melanism."

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: There are two opposing views about origin of modern man. According 10 one view Homo erectus in Asia were the ancestors of modern man. A study of variation of DNA however suggested African origin of modern man. What kind of observation on DNA variation could suggest this?
options: greater variation in Asia than in Africa
greater variation in Africa than in Asia
similar variation in Africa and Asia
variation only in Asia and no variation in Africa.
questions.solution:
There are two models about origin of modern man (Homo sapiens sapiens)
(i) Multiregional model: According to this view, modern humans evolved in many parts of the world from regional descendants of Homo erectus who dispersed from Africa between 1 and 2 million years ago.
(ii) Monogenesis model: According to this view, African descendents of Homo erectus gave rise to modern humans.
In late 1980s, Rebecca Cann and other geneticists supported this view on the basis of DNA of living humans. They compared the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) of a multiathenic sample of more than 100 people representing four continents. The greater the difference between the mtDNAs of two peoples, the longer ago that mtDNAs diverged from a common source. By using bioinformarics, they concluded that the divergence of mtDNA of Africans from common source began just 200, 000 years ago, much to late to represent the dispersal of Homo erectus. Thus, there are greater variation in Asia than in Africa.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: An important evidence in favour of organic evolution is the occurrence of:
questions.solution: An important evidence in favour of organic evolution is the occurrence of homologous and vestigial organs. Homologous organs have a common origin and are built on the same fundamental pattern, but they perform different functions and have different appearances. Vestigial organs in animals have no function now, but they had important functions in ancestors. Analogous organs are quite different in fundamental structure and embryonic origin but perform the same function. The study of analogous organs illustrates the occurrence of convergent evolution.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Evolutionary history of an organism is known as:
questions.solution:
Phylogeny pertains to the evolutionary history of a taxonomic group of organisms. Thus, phylogenetics is mainly concerned with the relationships of an organism to other organisms according to evolutionary similarities and differences. Ontogeny is the development of a single individual, or a system within the individual, from the fertilized egg to maturation and death. Ancestry represents persons initiating or comprising a line of descent. Palaeontology is the study of the history of life on Earth as based on fossils.
Related Theory
The biogenelic law was proposed by Ernst Haeckel which states that each embryo's developmental stage represents an adult form of an evolutionary ancestor i.e., an organism, in the course of its development, goes through all the stages of those forms oflife from which it has evolved.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following phenomena supports Darwin's concept of natural selection in organic evolution?
options: production of 'Dolly', the sheep by cloning
development of organs from 'stem cells' for organ transplantation.
questions.solution:
According to Darwin's theory of natural selection, The individual possessing useful variations survive whereas the others are eliminated. Nature selects the best suited and discards the others (survival of the fittest). Pesticide resistant insects are selected over pesticide sensitive insects by nature, and are thus survive through the course of evolution, until more suited (fittest) individual is selected, eliminating the former.
Related Theory
Darwinism can explain the survival of fittest but is unable to account for arrival of the fittest. It is difficult to suppose that small variations could have formed organs like wings and mimicry colouration which are useful only in their fully developed state but what about their presence in early stages.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What kind of evidence suggested that man is more closely related with chimpanzee than with at her hominoid apes?
options: evidence from DNA from sex chromosomes only
evidence from fossil remains, and the fossil mitochondrial DNA alone
evidence from DNA extracted from sex chromosomes, autosomes and mitochondria.
questions.solution:
Chimpanzee is more closely related to man than other hominoids. Chimpanzees are genetically closest to humans, and in fact, chimpanzees share about $98.6 \%$ of our DNA. Some similarities between human and chimpanzee in the chromosome banding pattern in sex chromosomes, autosomes and mitochondria. There is little difference in banding pattern in chromosomes 3 and 6 in human and chimpanzee. Serum test indicate maximum homology between human and chimpanzee.
Related Theory
Humans and monkeys are both primates. But humans are not descended from monkeys or any other primate living today. We do share a common ape ancestor with chimpanzees. It lived between 8 and 6 million years ago. They determined that chimpanzees are more closely related to humans than gorillas.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following amino-acids was not found to be synthesized in Miller's experiment?
questions.solution: Miller and Urey through their experiment abiotically synthesised amino acids and bases. They synthesised glycine, aspartic acid and alanine in abundant quantities. However, glutamic acid could not be synthesised in their experiment.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Adaptive radiation refers to:
options: evolution of different species from a common ancestor
migration of members of a species to different geographical areas
power of adaptation in an individual to a variety of environments
questions.solution: Adaptive radiation refers to evolution of different species from a common ancestor. It is the evolutionary process by which many species originate from one species in an area and radiate to different species. The mammals are adapted for different mode of life i.e., they show Adaptive radiation. They can be aerial (bat), aquatic(whale and dolphins), burrowing or fossorial (rat), cursorial (horse), or arboreal (monkey). The adaptive radiation is also known as Divergent evolution.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Diversification in plant life appeared:
options: due to long periods of evolutionary changes
questions.solution: Diversification in plant life appeared due to long periods of evolutionary changes. Earlier, the plants were thalloid and there were no differentiation among root, stem and leaves. Vascular tissues were absent as in alglae and bryophytes. In pteridophytes, seed habit was observed for the first time. Gymnosperm consists of vascular tissue and naked seed habitat. Angiosperms showed secondary growth, along with fruit formation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Convergent evolution is illustrated by:
questions.solution:
Convergent evolution occurs when species occupy similar ecological niches and adapt in similar ways in response to similar selective pressures. For example, Dogfish (Pisces) and whale (mammas) have acquired aquatic character though distantly related.
Rat and dog (mammals), bacterium and protozoan (unicellular), and starfish (mollusc) and cuttlefish (Echinodermata) show divergent evolution.
Related Theory
Sea stars do not have gills, scales, or fins. Sea stars live only in saltwater. Sea water, instead of blood, is actually used to pump nutrients through their bodies via a 'water vascular system. Hence, they are not considered as fish.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In recent years, DNA sequences (nucleotide sequence) of $m t$ DNA and Y chromosomes were considered for the study of human evolution, because:
options: they are small and therefore, easy to study
they are uniparental in origin and do not take part an recombination
their structure is known in greater detail
they can be studied from the samples of fossil remains
questions.solution:
Sequence of both $m t$ DNA and $\mathrm{Y}$ chromosomes are considered for the study of human evolution because they are uniparental in origin. mtDNA is inherited along with the maternal cytoplasm and $\mathrm{Y}$ chromosome is inherited from father. So they do not take part in recombination. In addition, mtDNA has a higher mutation rate then nuclear DNA so that it is more useful for short term evolutionary studies.
Related Theory
The Ychromosomeisinheritedfromthefather; therefore, paternal social class was included in the Y chromosome analysis. Mitochondrial DNA is inherited from the mother; thus, maternal social class was included in the analysis along with paternal social class for mitochondrial DNA. More than $27 \%$ of the variance in Y-haplogroups can be attributed to differences between populations, whereas mtDNA showed much lower heterogeneity between populations (less than 5\%), suggesting a strong influence of patrilocal social structure.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following describes correctly the homologous structures?
options: organs with anatomical similarities, but performing different functions
organs with anatomical dissimilarities, but performing same function
organs that have no function now, but had an important function in ancestors
organs appearing only in embryonic stage and disappearing later in the adult
questions.solution: The organs which have the same structure and origin but look different and perform different functions are called homologous organs. The organs which have the same function and are superficially alike but are quite different in their fundamental structure and embryonic origin are called analogous organs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Random genetic drift in a population probably results from:
questions.solution:
Genetic drift (Sewall Wright effect) is the random change in the frequency of alleles in a population over successive generations in the gametes. Each new generation differs from its parental generation with regard to allele frequencies simply because of random variation in the distribution of gametes. This process is more rapid in smaller populations, or when the alleles concerned confer no apparent benefit compared to their counterparts.
Related Theory
A founder effect occurs when a new colony is started by a few members of the original population. This small population size means that the colony may have reduced genetic variation from the original population and a non-random sample of the genes in the original population.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Some bacteria are able to grow in the streptomycin containing medium due to:
questions.solution: Bacteria are able to grow in a Streptomycin containing medium due to development of resistance to the bacteria by a process called natural selection. Normally bacteria cannot survive in antibiotic containing medium but if it does so it must have acquired resistance against that antibiotic. These are well adapted to grow in streptomycin containing medium and thus are more evolved. So due to natural selection only, the more evolved and better-adapted species is able to survive.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a population, unrestricted reproductive capacity is called as:
questions.solution:
Biotic Potential is defined as the physiological capacity of organisms to produce their offspring under natural and environmentally optimum conditions. Biotic potential is the highest possible vital index of a species; therefore, when the species has its highest birth rate and lowest mortality rate.
Related Theory:-
The sum of total inhibitory environmental factors, both biotic and abiotic, which regulate population size and do not permit unlimited growth of population is called environmental resistance. Because of environmental resistance, the populations are unable to reach full biotic potential.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following are homologous organs?
options: Wings of birds (sparrow) and pectoral fins of fish
questions.solution: Homologous organs are the ones that have a common and similar basic structure but perform different functions. The wings of a bird and fins of a fish have similarity in their basic anatomical structure (made of bony musculature) but the wings are used for flying whereas the fins are used for swimming.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Genetic drift operates in:
questions.solution: Genetic drift is changes in allele frequencies of a gene pool due to chance or random events. This can occur in large or small populations. It causes gene pools of two isolated populations to become dissimilar as some alleles are lost and other are fixed. However, It acts faster and has more drastic results in smaller populations. This effect is particularly important in rare and endangered species. Genetic drift can contribute to speciation. For example, a small isolated population may diverge from the larger population through genetic drift.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: According to fossils that are discovered up to present time, from which country the origin and evolution of man was started?
questions.solution: Modern humans originated in Africa 200,000 years ago and evolved from their most likely recent common ancestor, Homo erectus that lived between 1.9 million and 135,000 years ago.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In which era reptiles were dominated?
questions.solution: The Mesozoic era (Devonian period) is called the age of reptiles because this is when dinosaurs dominated the Earth. When a mass extinction occurred, it killed off all of the dinosaurs and was one of the largest in the history of the Earth.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is common to whale, seal and shark?
questions.solution: The analogous organs show convergent evolution due to similar adaptation. They do not support organic evolution. Distantly related animals (whale, seal and shark) inhabiting similar habitats of tendevelop similar morphological features which make them look similar. This is termed adaptive convergence or convergent evolution.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is the relatively most accurate method for dating of fossils?
questions.solution:
Electron spin resonance method is relatively most accurate method for dating fossils.
Electron spin resonance dating is a technique that can directly detect unpaired or odd electrons in atomic or molecular systems. In this technique, a static magnetic field and microwaves are used to observe the behavior of the unpaired electrons in the material being studied. The study of the behavior of the electrons in a sample gives information about the condition of the sample.

All mammals except whales and camels have seven cervical vertebrae
Darwinian variations are small and directionless.

Survival of the fittest is a result of selection and proliferation of only those organisms which were most suitably adapted to the environment and get selected by nature. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Jurassic period of the mesozoic era is characterised by:
options: flowering plants and first dinosaurs appear
gymnosperms are dominant plants and first birds appear
radiation of reptiles and origin of mammal like reptiles
dinosaurs become extinct and angiosperms appear
questions.solution: The Jurassic period is the second geological period of the Mesozoic era. In this period, the gymnosperms were dominant and the plants included ferns, cycads, Ginkgo, rushes and conifers; among animals, important invertebrates included ammonites, corals, brachiopods, bivalves and echinoids. Reptiles dominated the vertebrates and the first flying reptile, the pterosaurs appeared. The first primitive bird Archaeopteryx also made its appearance.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a random mating population in equilibrium, which one of the following brings about a change in gene frequency in a non-directional manner ?
questions.solution: In a random mating population in equilibrium, random drift brings about a change in gene frequency in a non-directional manner. Random drift is a non- directional factor.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following sequences was proposed by Darwin and Wallace for organic evolution?
options: overproduction, variations, constancy of population size, natural selection
variations, constancy of population size, overproduction, natural selection
overproduction, constancy of population size, variations, natural selection
variations, natural selection, overproduction,constancy of population size
questions.solution:
Overproduction, variations, the constancy of population size, natural selection sequence was proposed by Darwin and Wallace for organic evolution.
Overproduction: There is an overproduction of organisms due to high reproductive rate, even when the resources are limited. Even though the population increases enormously, the number of individuals in every generation remains constant.
Variation: means differences, like you have black and white peppered moths, red, green capsicum and hundreds of colours of butterflies. And they are all different because they are adapting themselves, to be better than each other.
Natural selection: It states that nature creates struggle and selects those animals which win in the competition. The organisms which have useful variations will win in the competition. Whereas the organisms which have no such useful variations will die.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Darwin in his "Natural Selection Theory" did not believe in any role of which one of the following in organic evolution ?
options: parasites and predators as natural enemies
questions.solution:
The theory of natural selection is based on the following factors :
(i) Rapid multiplication and limited food and space which leads to struggle for existence.
(ii) Struggle for existence and variations which leads to natural selection or survival of the fittest.
(iii) Natural selection and inheritance of useful variation over many generation which leads to formation of new species.
Darwin in his 'Natural Selection Theory did not believe in the role of discontinuous variation in natural selection. Darwin always believed in the universal occurrence of variation. In his opinion, variation is continuous in nature.
Related Theory
Because resources are limited in nature, organisms with heritable traits that favour survival and reproduction will tend to leave more offspring than their peers, causing the traits to increase in frequency over generations.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: One of the important consequences of geographical isolation is:
options: no change in the isolated fauna.
questions.solution:
Speciation is the evolutionary process for the formation of new species. The species diversity occurs when gene flow within the common pool is interrupted by an isolating mechanism.
Related Theory
The isolation can occur through geographical separation of population known as allopatric speciation. When a few individuals of a species within the same geographical area suddenly become reproductively isolated and form new species, it is known as sympatric speciation.

questions.q: What does the Big Bang theory describe?
questions.solution: Galaxies contain stars and clouds of gas and dust. Considering the size of universe, earth is indeed a speck. The Big Bang theory attempts to explain to us the origin of universe. It talks of a singular huge explosion unimaginable in physical terms. The universe expanded and hence, the temperature came down. Hydrogen and Helium formed sometime later. The gases condensed under gravitation and formed the galaxies of the present day universe. In the solar system of the milky way galaxy, earth was supposed to have been formed about 4.5 billion years back. There was no atmosphere on early earth. questions.q: During his journey, which island did Darwin visit that sparked his observations on evolution?

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the essence of the Darwinian theory about evolution?
questions.solution: The essence of Darwinian theory about evolution is natural selection. The rate of appearance of new forms is linked to the life cycle or the life span. Microbes that divide fast have the ability to multiply and become millions of individuals within hours. A colony of bacteria (say A) growing on a given medium has built-in variation in terms of ability to utilise a feed component. A change in the medium composition would bring out only that part of the population (say B) that can survive under the new conditions. In due course of time this variant population outgrows the others and appears as new species. This would happen within days. For the same thing to happen in a fish or fowl would take million of years as life spans of these animals are in years. Here we say that fitness of B is better than that of A under the new conditions. Nature selects for fitness. One must remember that the so-called fitness is based on characteristics which are inherited. Hence, there must be a genetic basis for getting selected and to evolve. Another way of saying the same thing is that some organisms are better adapted to survive in an otherwise hostile environment. Adaptive ability is inherited. It has a genetic basis. Fitness is the end result of the ability to adapt and get selected by nature.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Who proposed the idea that evolution of life forms occurred due to the use and disuse of organs?
questions.solution: Even before Darwin, a French naturalist Lamarck had said that evolution of life forms had occurred but driven by use and disuse of organs. He gave the examples of Giraffes who in an attempt to forage leaves on tall trees had to adapt by elongation of their necks. As they passed on this acquired character of elongated neck to succeeding generations, Giraffes, slowly, over the years, came to acquire long necks. Nobody believes this conjecture any more. Is evolution a process or the result of a process? The world we see,inanimate and animate, is only the success stories of evolution. When we describe the story of this world we describe evolution as a process. On the other hand when we describe the story of life on earth, we treat evolution as a consequence of a process called natural selection. We are still not very clear whether to regard evolution and natural selection as processes or end result of unknown processes.

questions.solution: When we look at stars on a clear night sky we are, in a way, looking back in time. Stellar distances are measured in light years. Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Early Greek thinkers thought units of life called spores were transferred to different planets including earth
2. Alfred Wallace by careful experimentation demonstrated that life comes only from pre-existing life
3. Oparin of Russia and Haldane of England proposed that the first form of life could have come from pre-existing non-living inorganic molecules
4. S.L. Miller observed formation of amino acids.
5. The first non-cellular forms of life could have originated 3 billion years back
questions.solution: Early Greek thinkers thought units of life called spores were transferred to different planets including earth. ‘Panspermia’ is still a favourite idea for some astronomers. For a long time it was also believed that life came out of decaying and rotting matter like straw, mud, etc. This was the theory of spontaneous generation. Louis Pasteur by careful experimentation demonstrated that life comes only from pre-existing life. He showed that in pre-sterilised flasks, life did not come from killed yeast while in another flask open to air, new living organisms arose from ‘killed yeast’. Spontaneous generation theory was dismissed once and for all. However, this did not answer how the first life form came on earth.

questions.subject: Zoology

1. All living organisms (species or types) that we see today were created as such.
2. The diversity was always the same since creation and will be the same in future also.
3. Earth is about 4000 years old.
4. Charles Darwin concluded that existing living forms share similarities to varying degrees not only among themselves but also with life forms that existed millions of years ago.
questions.solution: One, that all living organisms (species or types) that we see today were created as such. Two, that the diversity was always the same since creation and will be the same in future also. Three, that earth is about 4000 years old. All these ideas were strongly challenged during the nineteenth century. Based on observations made during a sea voyage in a sail ship called H.M.S. Beagle round the world, Charles Darwin concluded that existing living forms share similarities to varying degrees not only among themselves but also with life forms that existed millions of years ago. Many such life forms do not exist any more. There had been extinctions of different life forms in the years gone by just as new forms of life arose at different periods of history of earth. There has been gradual evolution of life forms.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:

1. The fitness, according to Darwin, does not refer to reproductive fitness
2. Those who are better fit in an environment, leave more progeny than others
3. All the existing life forms share similarities and share common ancestors.
4. These ancestors were present at different periods in the history of earth (epochs, periods and eras). 5. The geological history of earth closely correlates with the biological history of earth.
questions.solution: The fitness, according to Darwin, refers ultimately and only to reproductive fitness. Hence, those who are better fit in an environment, leave more progeny than others. These, therefore, will survive more and hence are selected by nature. He called it natural selection and implied it as a mechanism of evolution. Let us also remember that Alfred Wallace, a naturalist who worked in Malay Archipelago had also come to similar conclusions around the same time. In due course of time, apparently new types of organisms are recognisable. All the existing life forms share similarities and share common ancestors. However, these ancestors were present at different periods in the history of earth (epochs, periods and eras). The geological history of earth closely correlates with the biological history of earth. A common permissible conclusion is that earth is very old, not thousand of years as was thought earlier but billions of years old.

questions.solution: Embryological support for evolution was also proposed by Ernst Heckel based upon the observation of certain features during embryonic stage common to all vertebrates that are absent in adult. For example, the embryos of all vertebrates including human develop a row of vestigial gill slit just behind the head but it is a functional organ only in fish and not found in any other adult vertebrates. However, this proposal was disapproved on careful study performed by Karl Ernst von Baer. He noted that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals

2. Homology indicates common ancestry.

4. The eye of the octopus and of mammals or the flippers of Penguins and Dolphins are analogous structures
5. Vertebrate hearts or brains are homologous structures
questions.solution: Homology is based on divergent evolution whereas analogy refers to a situation exactly opposite. Wings of butterfly and of birds look alike. They are not anatomically similar structures though they perform similar functions. Hence, analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution - different structures evolving for the same function and hence having similarity. Other examples of analogy are the eye of the octopus and of mammals or the flippers of Penguins and Dolphins. One can say that it is the similar habitat that has resulted in selection of similar adaptive features in different groups of organisms but toward the same function: Sweet potato (root modification) and potato (stem modification) is another example for analogy

However, in the collection carried out from the same area, but after industrialisation, i.e., in 1920, there were more dark-winged moths in the same area, i.e., the proportion was reversed.

4. Theoretically population size will grow in a limited manner if everybody reproduced maximally
questions.solution: The essence of Darwinian theory about evolution is natural selection. The rate of appearance of new forms is linked to the life cycle or the life span. Microbes that divide fast have the ability to multiply and become millions of individuals within hours. A colony of bacteria (say A) growing on a given medium has built-in variation in terms of ability to utilise a feed component. A change in the medium composition would bring out only that part of the population (say B) that can survive under the new conditions. In due course of time this variant population outgrows the others and appears as new species. This would happen within days.

questions.solution: What is the origin of this variation and how does speciation occur? Even though Mendel had talked of inheritable 'factors' influencing phenotype, Darwin either ignored these observations or kept silence. In the first decade of twentieth century, Hugo deVries based on his work on evening primrose brought forth the idea of mutations – large difference arising suddenly in a population. He believed that it is mutation which causes evolution and not the minor variations (heritable) that Darwin talked about. Mutations are random and directionless while Darwinian variations are small and directional. Evolution for Darwin was gradual while deVries believed mutation caused speciation and hence called it saltation (single step large mutation). Studies in population genetics, later, brought out some clarity.

questions.solution: In a given population one can find out the frequency of occurrence of alleles of a gene or a locus. This frequency is supposed to remain fixed and even remain the same through generations. Hardy-Weinberg principle stated it using algebraic equations. This principle says that allele frequencies in a population are stable and is constant from generation to generation. The gene pool (total genes and their alleles in a population) remains a constant. This is called genetic equilibrium.

4. Natural selection is a process in which heritable variations enabling better survival are enabled to reproduce and leave lesser number of progeny.

questions.solution: Five factors are known to affect Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. These are gene migration or gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination and natural selection. When migration of a section of population to another place and population occurs, gene frequencies change in the original as well as in the new population. New genes/alleles are added to the new population and these are lost from the old population. There would be a gene flow if this gene migration, happens multiple times. If the same change occurs by chance, it is called genetic drift. Sometimes the change in allele frequency is so different in the new sample of population that they become a different species. The original drifted population becomes founders and the effect is called founder effect.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:

(A) When more than one adaptive radiation appeared to have occurred in an isolated geographical area, it leads to convergent evolution.
(B) Darwin's finches and Australian marsupials are both classic examples of adaptive radiation.
(C) Lemur and Spotted cuscus are examples of divergent evolution.
(D) Placental wolf and Tasmanian wolf share a recent common ancestor.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct. According to NCERT, when more than one adaptive radiation occurs in an isolated geographical area representing different habitats, it is called convergent evolution.

Statement (B) is correct. Both Darwin's finches in the Galapagos Islands and marsupials in Australia evolved from a single ancestral stock into various forms, which is the definition of adaptive radiation.

Statement (C) is incorrect. Lemur (a placental mammal) and Spotted cuscus (an Australian marsupial) evolved independently to occupy similar ecological niches, which is an example of convergent evolution, not divergent evolution.

Statement (D) is incorrect. Placental wolf and Tasmanian wolf do not share a recent common ancestor. They belong to entirely different mammalian lineages (placental and marsupial) but show phenotypic similarities due to convergent evolution.

Thus, exactly two statements, (A) and (B), are correct.

Answer: Two

Ernst Haeckel proposed embryological support for evolution based on the observation that all vertebrate embryos share certain features that are absent in adults.

However, Karl Ernst von Baer performed careful studies and disapproved this proposal. He observed that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals.

Thus, the Assertion is a correct historical fact from evolutionary biology, and the Reason provides the exact scientific observation made by von Baer that led to the disapproval of Haeckel's proposal.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are correct, and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution:

Divergent evolution results in homologous structures, which share a common ancestry but perform different functions (e.g., forelimbs of whales and bats).

Convergent evolution results in analogous structures, which perform similar functions but have different anatomical origins (e.g., wings of butterfly and birds).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (I), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III).

B. Forelimbs of bat and cheetahII. Convergent evolution
C. Darwin's finchesIII. Divergent evolution
D. Biochemical similarities in proteinsIV. Evidence for common ancestry


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The eye of an octopus and a mammal differ in their anatomical structure but perform the same function of vision. They are analogous structures resulting from convergent evolution (A-II).

The forelimbs of a bat and a cheetah share the same fundamental bone structure but are adapted for different functions (flying and running). They are homologous structures resulting from divergent evolution (B-III).

Darwin's finches represent the evolution of different species from a common ancestor in a given geographical area, which is adaptive radiation (C-I).

Biochemical similarities in proteins and genes among diverse organisms indicate shared ancestry, providing evidence for common ancestry (D-IV).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The forelimbs of whales, bats, cheetahs, and humans share similarities in the pattern of bones but perform different functions. Select the correct combination of terms to explain this evolutionary relationship.
questions.solution:

Homologous organs arise due to divergent evolution, where the same structure developed along different directions due to adaptations to different needs. Confusing homology with convergent evolution or analogy is a common mistake.

Answer: Homology, divergent

Flippers of penguins and dolphins are an example of convergent evolution (analogous structures).

Antibiotic-resistant bacteria represent evolution by anthropogenic action.

questions.subject: Zoology

options: Convergent evolution driven by identical environmental pressures

Divergent evolution from a shared common ancestor
Adaptive radiation occurring without common ancestry
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, similarities in proteins and genes performing a given function among diverse organisms give clues to common ancestry. These biochemical similarities point to the same shared ancestry as structural similarities (homology) among diverse organisms.

Both biochemical and structural homologies provide evidence for divergent evolution, where different groups evolve from a shared common ancestor. Convergent evolution leads to analogous structures, not homologous ones, and adaptive radiation implies evolution from a common ancestor in a given geographical area.

Answer: Divergent evolution from a shared common ancestor

It is not considered atavism because atavism involves the sudden and rare reappearance of a trait that had completely disappeared in the immediate ancestors (such as the birth of a baby with a short tail). Therefore, the definitions provided in the Reason correctly explain why the appendix is classified as vestigial rather than atavistic.

questions.q: The placental flying squirrel and the marsupial flying phalanger have both evolved membranous extensions for gliding in their respective forest habitats. Identify the type of evolution shown by them and the nature of their gliding structures.
questions.solution:

They have developed similar phenotypic adaptations (membranous extensions for gliding) to survive in similar forest habitats. This independent evolution of similar features in different lineages is termed convergent evolution.

Structures that evolve through convergent evolution perform similar functions but have different anatomical origins and are not derived from a common ancestor. Such structures are called analogous structures.

Answer: Convergent evolution and Analogous structures

questions.solution:

Darwin finches represent a single adaptive radiation. Wings of butterfly and bird show convergent evolution but do not represent the specific case of multiple converging adaptive radiations. Forelimbs of whale and bat are homologous structures representing divergent evolution.

Neanderthal man had a brain size of $1400\text{ cc}$ and used hides to protect their body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of mammals is an example of divergent evolution?
questions.solution:
Adaptive radiation is a process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and radiating to other areas of geography, which is a form of divergent evolution. A number of marsupials, each different from the other, evolved from an ancestral stock within the Australian island continent. Tasmanian wolf and Tiger cat are both Australian marsupials, thus representing divergent evolution from a common marsupial ancestor.

When more than one adaptive radiation appears to have occurred in an isolated geographical area (representing different habitats), it results in convergent evolution. Lemur (placental) and Spotted cuscus (marsupial), Flying squirrel (placental) and Flying phalanger (marsupial), and Wolf (placental) and Tasmanian wolf (marsupial) are pairs representing convergent evolution.

Answer: Tasmanian wolf and Tiger cat

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Fossils discovered in Java in 1891 revealed a distinct stage in human evolution. Which of the following represents the characteristic features of the hominid that appeared chronologically immediately after this stage?
options: They had a brain capacity between 650-800 cc and probably did not eat meat.
They had a large brain around 900 cc and probably ate meat.
They arose in Africa, moved across continents and developed prehistoric cave art.
They had a brain size of 1400 cc and used hides to protect their body.
questions.solution:
The fossils discovered in Java in 1891 belong to Homo erectus, who lived about 1.5 million years ago.
According to the chronological sequence of human evolution, the hominid that appeared after Homo erectus is Neanderthal man (lived near east and central Asia between 1,00,000-40,000 years back).
Neanderthal man had a brain size of 1400 cc, used hides to protect their body and buried their dead.

Option 1 describes Homo habilis, which appeared before Homo erectus.
Option 2 describes Homo erectus itself.
Option 3 describes Homo sapiens, which appeared after Neanderthal man.

Answer: They had a brain size of 1400 cc and used hides to protect their body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: When more than one adaptive radiation appeared to have occurred in an isolated geographical area (representing different habitats), the resulting evolutionary pattern is known as:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, when more than one adaptive radiation appeared to have occurred in an isolated geographical area (representing different habitats), one can call this convergent evolution. A classic example is the similarity between placental mammals and Australian marsupials, where each group underwent its own adaptive radiation but evolved similar forms to occupy similar ecological niches.

Divergent evolution is typically associated with a single adaptive radiation from a common ancestor.

Saltation refers to a single-step large mutation as proposed by Hugo de Vries.

Answer: Convergent evolution

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Reason (R) is false because although Homo habilis had a brain capacity of 650-800 cc, they probably did not eat meat.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sweet potato and potato represent convergent evolution.
Reason (R): They share a similar anatomical origin and structure but perform different functions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.solution:
Sweet potato is a root modification and potato is a stem modification. They have different anatomical origins but perform the same function of food storage. This makes them analogous organs, which are a result of convergent evolution. Therefore, Assertion (A) is correct.

Reason (R) is incorrect because analogous organs have different anatomical origins and perform similar functions. The statement in the reason describes homologous organs (divergent evolution), not analogous ones.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A paleontologist discovers a fossilized rock stratum containing abundant fossils of seed ferns and early amphibians, but completely lacking any fossils of true reptiles and angiosperms. Based on the evolutionary history of flora and fauna, this rock stratum most likely belongs to which geological period?
questions.solution:
According to the geological time scale and evolutionary history in NCERT, seed ferns and amphibians were prominent during the Carboniferous period.

True reptiles evolved later and diversified in the Permian and Mesozoic eras, while angiosperms evolved much later in the Cretaceous period. The Devonian period is known as the age of fishes and predates the dominance of seed ferns. Therefore, the presence of seed ferns and amphibians without true reptiles strongly indicates the Carboniferous period.

Answer: Carboniferous

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Reason (R): Mammals originated in the Cenozoic era immediately following the mass extinction of dinosaurs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. Following the extinction of dinosaurs at the end of the Mesozoic era, mammals underwent adaptive radiation and became the dominant land animals during the Cenozoic era, which is why it is called the 'Age of Mammals'.

Reason (R) is false. Mammals did not originate in the Cenozoic era. They first appeared earlier, during the Triassic period of the Mesozoic era, and coexisted with dinosaurs for millions of years before eventually dominating in the Cenozoic.

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Read the following statements regarding the geological time scale and evolutionary history, and select the incorrect statement.

The Cenozoic era is divided into the Tertiary and Quaternary periods.
questions.solution:

The Mesozoic era began much later and is correctly identified as the age of reptiles (Statement 2). The Paleozoic era correctly includes the Silurian, Devonian, Carboniferous, and Permian periods (Statement 1), and the Cenozoic era correctly consists of the Tertiary and Quaternary periods (Statement 4).

Answer: Jawless fish probably evolved and flourished during the Mesozoic era.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:

Reason (R): The cranial capacity of Homo erectus was significantly smaller than that of Homo habilis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution:
According to the fossil record of human evolution, Homo habilis appeared about 2 million years ago, followed by Homo erectus around 1.5 million years ago. Thus, the Assertion is true.

The cranial capacity of Homo habilis was between 650-800 cc, whereas Homo erectus had a larger brain of around 900 cc. Therefore, the Reason is false because the cranial capacity of Homo erectus was larger, not smaller, than that of Homo habilis.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Sweet potato and potato perform a similar function of food storage but differ in their structural origin.

Which of the following options correctly identifies the type of evolution they represent and their respective anatomical origins?
options: Divergent evolution; both are modified stems
Convergent evolution; Sweet potato is a modified stem and potato is a modified root
Convergent evolution; Sweet potato is a modified root and potato is a modified stem
Divergent evolution; Sweet potato is a modified root and potato is a modified stem
questions.solution:
Sweet potato is a modified adventitious root, whereas potato is a modified underground stem. Because they have different anatomical origins but have evolved to perform the same function (storage of food), they are analogous structures.

Analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution, where different structures evolve similarly in response to similar environmental needs or functions.

Answer: Convergent evolution; Sweet potato is a modified root and potato is a modified stem

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
During embryonic development, all vertebrates including humans develop a row of vestigial gill slits just behind the head. This structure is functional only in fishes and is not found in other adult vertebrates.

Which scientist used this specific observation to propose embryological support for evolution, and what was the fundamental flaw in their conclusion as identified later?
options: Karl Ernst von Baer; the flaw was his conclusion that human embryos pass through an adult fish stage.
Ernst Haeckel; the flaw was his assumption that vestigial organs have no function in any vertebrate.
Ernst Haeckel; the flaw was his assumption that embryos pass through the adult stages of other animals.
Karl Ernst von Baer; the flaw was his assumption that gill slits are functional in human embryos.
questions.solution:
Ernst Haeckel proposed embryological support for evolution based on the observation that all vertebrate embryos develop certain common features, such as a row of vestigial gill slits, which are absent in adults.

However, Karl Ernst von Baer disapproved this proposal after careful study. Von Baer pointed out the fundamental flaw in Haeckel's reasoning: embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals. Therefore, the similarities in embryonic stages do not mean that higher vertebrate embryos represent the adult forms of lower vertebrates.

Answer: Ernst Haeckel; the flaw was his assumption that embryos pass through the adult stages of other animals.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The hearts and brains of different vertebrates exhibit a similar basic structural plan despite varying degrees of complexity. What type of organs do they represent, and which evolutionary phenomenon do they indicate?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, vertebrate hearts and brains share the same fundamental structural plan and embryonic origin but have evolved to exhibit varying degrees of complexity. Such organs are classified as homologous organs.

Homologous structures arise due to divergent evolution, where the same basic structure develops along different directions as adaptations to different needs.

Analogous organs, on the other hand, arise due to convergent evolution and have different anatomical origins but similar functions.

Answer: Homologous organs, Divergent evolution

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The phenotypic similarity observed between the Placental wolf and the Tasmanian wolf is attributed to which of the following evolutionary processes?
questions.solution:
The Placental wolf is a placental mammal, whereas the Tasmanian wolf is an Australian marsupial. They belong to entirely different evolutionary lineages but show striking phenotypic similarities. This occurs because they adapted to similar ecological niches in isolated geographical areas, a process known as convergent evolution.

Divergent evolution leads to homologous structures among related organisms sharing a common ancestor. Co-evolution involves two interacting species evolving together, and artificial selection is driven by human breeding.

Answer: Convergent evolution

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of biological examples and their corresponding evolutionary mechanisms is incorrectly matched?
options: Eye of octopus and mammals → Convergent evolution
Vertebrate hearts and brains → Convergent evolution
Antibiotic-resistant bacteria → Evolution by anthropogenic action
questions.solution:
Vertebrate hearts and brains share a similar basic structural plan but have been modified to perform different functions in different vertebrate classes. They are homologous organs and represent divergent evolution, not convergent evolution.

The eye of an octopus and mammals differ in their basic structure but perform the same function, representing convergent evolution.

Australian marsupials are a classic example of adaptive radiation, where multiple species evolved from a common ancestor in an isolated geographical area.

The development of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is a direct result of excessive use of antibiotics by humans, which is an example of evolution by anthropogenic action.

Answer: Vertebrate hearts and brains → Convergent evolution

questions.subject: Zoology

Assertion (A): Flippers of penguins and dolphins are considered homologous structures.
Reason (R): They have different anatomical origins but evolved to perform similar functions due to convergent evolution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
The Assertion is false because the flippers of penguins (birds) and dolphins (mammals) are analogous structures, not homologous. They do not share a common ancestor with these specific flipper structures.

The Reason is true. Analogous structures arise when organisms with different anatomical origins adapt to similar habitats or lifestyles, evolving structures that perform similar functions (like swimming in this case). This evolutionary process is known as convergent evolution.

Therefore, Assertion is false but Reason is true.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not an example of convergent evolution ?
options: Fore limbs of whales and bats
questions.solution:
Convergent evolution is the process by which unrelated or distantly related organisms evolve similar structures or adaptations due to similar environmental pressures. These structures are called analogous organs.

Flippers of penguins and dolphins, eyes of octopuses and mammals, and wings of butterflies and birds are all examples of analogous organs, representing convergent evolution.

Forelimbs of whales and bats share the same fundamental anatomical bone structure (humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, and phalanges) but are adapted to perform different functions (swimming and flying, respectively). These are homologous organs, which represent divergent evolution.

Therefore, the forelimbs of whales and bats are not an example of convergent evolution.

questions.q: A population of diploid organisms is at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. If the frequency of allele A is $0.1$, the frequency of AA is __________.
questions.solution:

Given $p = 0.1$.

Frequency of AA $= p^2 = (0.1)^2 = 0.01$.

Answer: $0.01$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Natural selection can lead to __________.
(a) stabilisation
(b) genetic drift
(c) directional change
(d) disruption
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Natural selection is a process in which individuals with favorable inherited traits are more likely to survive and reproduce. Based on the traits favored, natural selection can lead to three main types of changes in a population.

Stabilisation occurs when more individuals acquire the mean character value, reducing variation.

Directional change occurs when more individuals acquire a value other than the mean character value, shifting the peak in one direction.

Disruption occurs when more individuals acquire peripheral character values at both ends of the distribution curve, leading to two peaks.

Genetic drift is a random change in allele frequencies, which is a separate evolutionary force and not a result of natural selection.

Therefore, natural selection can lead to stabilisation, directional change, and disruption.

Answer: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.solution:
Mechanism Definition and Examples
Adaptive radiation The process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and literally radiating to other areas of geography (habitats) is called adaptive radiation. Example: Darwin finches
Divergent evolution The structures in different organisms which have similarities in their anatomy or basic plan but serve different functions are known as homologous structures. This is an example of divergent evolution. Example: Bones of forelimbs in man and whale
Convergent evolution The structures in different organisms which are not similar anatomically though they perform similar functions are called analogous organs. This is an example of convergent evolution. Example: Wings of butterfly and bird
Evolution by anthropogenic action Herbicide and pesticide resistance developed in the weeds and pests respectively after prolonged use of herbicides and pesticides. This is also an example of natural selection which supports the process of evolution due to anthropogenic action or due to actions of man.

questions.solution: Based on the hypothesis proposed by Oparin and Haldane, S.L. Miller provided experimental evidence of the chemical evolution in 1953 in a laboratory set-up. S.L. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A gene locus has two alleles A, a. If the frequency of dominant allele A is 0.4, then what will be the frequency of homozygous dominant, heterozygous and homozygous recessive individuals in the Population?
questions.solution:
According to the Hardy-Weinberg principle: 

Frequency of dominant allele (A) = p =0.4

Frequency of recessive allele (a) = q

Sum total of all the allelic frequencies is 1, i.e. p+q = 1 

⇒  0.4 + q = 1 

⇒  q = 0.6                                    

Frequency of AA individuals = p × p = p2 = (0.4)2 = 0.16

Frequency of aa individuals = q × q = q2 = (0.6)2 = 0.36

Frequency of Aa individuals = 2pq = 2(0.4)(0.6) = 0.48

questions.q: According to Hugo de Vries, the mechanism of evolution is
questions.solution:
According to Hugo de Vries, the mechanism of evolution is saltation.
Hugo de Vries (1901) proposed the mutation theory of evolution and stated that evolution is a jerky process in which new species are evolved due to discontinuous sudden variations or saltation. These are the single step large mutations occurring in the population.
de Vries believed that evolution was a result of larger mutations opposed to Darwin's minor heritable variations or phenotypic variations. As mentioned, these mutations are achieved in a single step rather than multiple.

Analogous organs show convergent evolution. These organs have similar functions but are different in their structural details and origin. Development of different functional structures from a common ancestral form is called adaptive radiation.

questions.solution:
The structures in different organisms which are not similar anatomically though they perform similar functions are called as analogous organs. Morphologically they may or may not be similar which means that analogous structures may or may not look alike externally. The property of bearing analogous structures is called analogy. The analogous structures do not exhibit common origin. Unlike homology which indicates common ancestry, the analogy does not indicate common ancestry.

The wings of butterfly and of birds. Butterflies are the invertebrates whereas birds are vertebrates. The wings in both of them perform the common function of flying but the internal designs and components of these two types of wings are very different from one another. The wings look alike externally because they have a common use of flying. It is an example of convergent evolution.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A population will not exist in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium if:

The Hardy-Weinberg principle says that allele frequencies in a population are stable and constant from generation to generation as long as

  • The population is large enough and changes in allele frequencies due to chance or accident are insignificant. 
  • Mating occurs at random. 
  • Mutation does not occur or if it does occur it must reach a state of equilibrium. 
  • All the members of the population survive and have equal reproductive rates.

A population will not exist in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium if the individuals mate selectively as the mating has to be random and influences like mutation, natural selection and genetic drift affect the equilibrium.

questions.solution:
Analogous structures are those organs which are structurally different, but they perform the same set of functions. Of the given pairs of structures, the gills of prawns and lungs of man are analogous in nature. Both of these are respiratory structures, which are anatomically different from each others. The lungs of man are balloon-like sac organs which inflate and deflate on breathing, while gills of prawn are crescent-shaped organs which perform gas exchange for respiration.

Wings of bat and wings of pigeon have anatomically similar structures as well as they perform the same function of flying. Hence, it is difficult to strictly mark them as analogous or homologous.

The other two examples exhibit homology. That is, they are structurally the same, but they perform different functions.

Related Theory
Darwin studied the climatic conditions, fauna and flora of Galapagos islands. He noticed varieties of small birds in these islands which differed mainly in the shape and size of their beak and in the colour of their plumage. These birds are now called Darwin's finches. Darwin concluded that the American mainland species was the original one from which different forms migrated to the different islands of Galapagos and adapted to the different environmental conditions of these islands. These adapted forms are considered to be the new species. Thus, Darwin's finches provide a beautiful example of adaptive radiation supporting the concept of evolution.

questions.solution:
Genetic variation in a population Arise due to reshuffling of genes caused by recombination and mutations. Recombination occurs due to formation of synapsis during crossing over in cell division, while mutation are sudden heritable changes in the sequence of genome. Reproductive isolation and selection do not cause variation, as due to this, selective genome cause inheritance of similar traits in offspring.
Related Theory
According to Hugo de Vries mutation theory. new species arise suddenly showing abrupt deviations in characters from the normal forms. Thus, evolution is not a slow and gradual process but a sudden discontinuous and jerky process. The mutation theory differs from Darwin's theory in the nature of the variations, whereas continuous variations are the raw materials for the formation of new species in Darwin's theory of natural selection; but in De Vries theory. discontinuous variation or mutations are the raw materials.

questions.solution:

- When mating is random in a large population with no disruptive circumstances, both genotype and allele frequencies will remain constant because they are in equilibrium.
- Any factor, which can disturb the alleles in a population is likely to affect the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.

So, the correct answer is 'Natural selection'.

questions.solution:
There are two models about origin of modern man (Homo sapiens sapiens) i.e.
(i) Multiregional model : According to this view, Modern humans evolved in many parts of the world from regional descendants of Homo erectus who dispersed from Africa between 1 and 2 million years ago.
(ii) Monogenesis model: According to this view only African descendents of Homo erectus gave rise to modern humans. In late 1980s Rebecca Cann and other geneticists supported this view on the basis of DNA of living humans. They compared the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) of a multiathenic sample of more than 100 people representing four continents. The greater the difference between the mtDNAs of two peoples, the longer ago that mtDNAs diverged from a common source. By using bioinformatics, they concluded that the divergence of $m t$ DNA of Africans from common source began just 200,000 years ago, much to late to represent the dispersal of Homo erectus. Thus there are greater variation in Asia than in Africa.

questions.q: Using imprints from a plate with complete medium and carrying bacterial colonies, you can select streptomycin resistant mutants and prove that such mutations do not originate as adaptation. These imprints need to be used
options: on plates with and without streptomycin
questions.solution: Plates having streptomycin allow to propagate only those bacteria, which are resistant to the antibiotic.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which have not left any evidences of organic evolution?
questions.solution:
The organisms which possess the characters of two different groups are called connecting links. They provide the evidence of organic evolution.
Examples :
(1) Archaeopteryx is connecting link between reptiles and birds.
(2) Neopilina is connecting link between Annelida and Mollusca.
(3) Peripatus is connecting link between Annelida and Arthropoda.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Organs which differ in origin but perform similar functions :
questions.solution:
The organs which have similar function but are different in their structure and origin are called analogous organs.
The organs which have same fundamental structure and origin but function may be similar or different, are called homologous organs.
The organs which are present in reduced form and do not correspond to the fully developed functional organs to related animals are called vestigial organs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Set which includes only analogous organs is :
options: wings of butterfly, housefly and bat
hindlegs of horse, grasshopper and bat
wings of butterfly and wingspread of bat and birds
mandibles of cockroach, mosquito and honey bee
questions.solution:
Analogous organs have similar functions but are different in their structure and origin.
Examples :
(1) Wings of butterfly, birds and bat have similar functions.
(2) Stings of honey bee and scorpion are analogous structures.
(3) Fins of fishes and flippers of whales are analogous organs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: 'Convergent Evolution' is shown by :
questions.solution: Convergent evolution or adaptive convergence or parallel evolution is shown by analogous organs, whereas divergent evolution or evolutionary divergence or adaptive radiation are shown by homologous organs.

questions.solution: Wings of bird and insects are analogous organs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following is vestigeal organ of human?
questions.solution: Vestigeal organs are present in reduced form and are of no use to the animal in which they are present. Man has, 180 vestigeal organs. e.g., nictitating membrane, vermiform appendix, wisdom tooth, muscle of pinna and forhead, mammary glands in male etc.
